questions.prompt: With your U03 code closed: what does the TypeScript compiler actually guarantee about external JSON, and what must still happen at runtime?

keyPoints.text: TypeScript checks assumptions before the program runs; JavaScript is what actually executes
keyPoints.quote: JavaScript is the runtime; TypeScript checks assumptions before execution.

keyPoints.text: An annotation alone never validates JSON that arrives from outside
keyPoints.quote: Type annotations do not validate external JSON.

keyPoints.text: External input starts as unknown and is inspected and narrowed into a trusted type
keyPoints.quote: Treat external input as unknown, inspect it and narrow to a trusted type.

keyPoints.text: A discriminated union models alternatives without contradictory boolean flags
keyPoints.quote: A discriminated union expresses alternatives without contradictory boolean flags.

keyPoints.text: any and unchecked assertions hide exactly the runtime check that is missing
keyPoints.quote: Avoid any and unchecked assertions that hide a missing runtime check.

keyPoints.text: Only validation at the boundary lets the compiler trust a network response's shape
keyPoints.quote: The compiler cannot prove a network response has this shape unless the boundary validates it.

questions.prompt: Spell out the parseTask boundary contract: which inputs are rejected, which boundary values need explicit checks, and what is forbidden in the implementation?

keyPoints.text: The title is trimmed and must be nonempty and at most 80 characters, with minutes an integer from 1 to 240
keyPoints.quote: Trim title, require nonempty <=80 characters and integer minutes 1–240.

keyPoints.text: null, arrays and wrong types are rejected while unknown fields are ignored and the input preserved
keyPoints.quote: Reject null, arrays and wrong types; ignore unknown fields and preserve input.

keyPoints.text: The boundary values 1, 240, 0, 241 and a whitespace-only title each get an explicit check
keyPoints.quote: Add checks for 1,240,0,241 and whitespace-only title.

keyPoints.text: No any and no unchecked as assertion; you should be able to explain the narrowing
keyPoints.quote: Use no any or unchecked as assertion; explain narrowing.

keyPoints.text: The delayed transfer applies the same narrowing to a book request with an optional integer page count
keyPoints.quote: Validate a book request with a title and optional integer page count.

keyPoints.text: Checking the discriminant kind is what narrows the union in the worked example

questions.prompt: What makes a test trustworthy in U03's terms? Contrast unit and integration tests, and say what mocks and coverage do not prove.

keyPoints.text: Tests verify what callers can see: ordinary cases, boundaries and failures
keyPoints.quote: Tests should verify caller-visible behavior: ordinary cases, boundaries and failures.

keyPoints.text: Unit tests isolate single decisions while integration tests exercise real components together
keyPoints.quote: Unit tests isolate decisions; integration tests check real components working together.

keyPoints.text: Passing against a mock says nothing certain about the real dependency's behavior
keyPoints.quote: A mock does not prove that its real dependency behaves the same way.

keyPoints.text: Time and randomness become explicit inputs so decisions stay testable
keyPoints.quote: Make time and randomness explicit inputs when testing decisions.

keyPoints.text: High coverage by itself does not show the assertions catch meaningful failures
keyPoints.quote: Coverage alone does not establish that assertions detect meaningful failures.
